AfterObtained.rationale: NutritiousOyster.cs:19 is `CreatureCmd.GainMaxHp(Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.MaxHp.BaseValue)`, and GainMaxHp is SetMaxHp(max + amount) followed by Heal(amount) (CreatureCmd.cs:786-799) -- the max-HP bump AND an equal heal. run.gain_max_hp does exactly that (`self.max_hp += amount; self.heal(amount)`). EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b10.py nutritious): a player at 60/80 becomes 71/91. The MapPointHistoryEntry.MaxHpGained bookkeeping at CreatureCmd.cs:793-797 is the game's own save writing, which the sim's conformance layer reads rather than writes. Rule 7: CreatureCmd.cs and run.py are unhashed here.

guards.what: G1: the port implements no `undo_after_obtained`, so the conformance runner cannot un-grant the +11 Max HP
guards.rationale: MECHANISM: undo_after_obtained (relics/base.py:143-151) has NO C# counterpart -- nothing in the game un-picks a relic -- and exists solely for the conformance runner, which auto-grants a node's relic and then swaps it for the one the save says was really picked (conformance/runner.py:451-466 and :683-701, both of which call relic.undo_after_obtained on the drop). Its own docstring names the exact failure: 'a discarded max-HP relic (Mango, Pear, ...) leaves its +MaxHp behind and the player-state parity check reads high for the rest of the run'. This relic mutates max_hp AND hp and supplies no undo. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b10.py nutritious): 60/80 -> add_relic -> 71/91 -> undo_after_obtained -> still 71/91. Five relics DO implement it and every one is a max-HP relic (executed: `grep -rn 'def undo_after_obtained' sts2_rl/relics/` returns lees_waffle, looming_fruit, mango, pear, strawberry), so this is an omission against the sim's own house pattern rather than a design choice. DORMANT rather than live, and the trigger is named precisely: Nutritious Oyster is granted only at the Neow node, so it fires on any conformance seed where the sim's Neow choice lands on this relic and the save's did not -- the node itself is visited by every run, unlike relic/fake_mango's Fake Merchant, but I did not run a conformance seed to observe it, so I am not labelling it live. CROSS-RECORD DISAGREEMENT UNDER BINDING RULE 3, reported and not resolved by me: relic/fake_mango N2 verdicts an identical missing undo on a max-HP relic as `gap`, while relic/golden_pearl N3 and relic/jewelry_box N3 verdict a missing undo as `faithful` on the grounds that there is no C# counterpart -- even though golden_pearl's own rationale predicts 'a spurious floor_gold diff of exactly 150'. I match fake_mango, as the closest analogue (a max-HP relic on the same code path), and have flagged the conflict in .superpowers/sdd/relic-batch-10-lessons.md for the stream owner to settle in one direction. Rule 7: relics/base.py, conformance/runner.py, relics/fake_mango.py, relics/golden_pearl.py, relics/jewelry_box.py and the five undo-implementing relic files are NOT hashed by this record. RULE-3 RESOLUTION (stream owner, 2026-07-26, after batch 10 flagged the conflict): the ABSENCE of undo_after_obtained is verdicted `faithful` at every site. undo_after_obtained has no C# counterpart -- nothing in the game un-picks a relic -- so a sim that does not implement it is not diverging from the source, which is the only question this audit asks. It is NOT a waiver either: a waiver means in-scope-adjacent and declined (multiplayer, ascension), whereas here there is no source behaviour to be faithful to. Five records had already reached `faithful` and two `gap`; the two are corrected here. The operational concern is REAL and is deliberately left in this entry's text -- a missing undo breaks the conformance runner's relic-swap and its DETECTOR 3 HP assertion -- but it is a tooling defect, not a fidelity gap. Distinct mechanism, still a gap wherever it applies: an undo_after_obtained that EXISTS and clamps instead of subtracting (mango G1, lees_waffle N4, looming_fruit N3) violates its own stated contract and stays `gap`.
